sense.text:
“That which he laboured for shall he restore, and shall not swallow it down”. Everything the white man is labouring for, all the gold he is storing up on the earth today, he shall restore, and he will not enjoy it. “according to his substance shall the restitution be”: according to all his gold and pearls and rubies and diamonds. That is going to be our restitution. When Christ returns, all the gold and all the wealth the white man has, he has to give to us. That is the restitution. That is righteous judgment.

This is the answer to the Pope apologizing for the Vatican’s role in legitimizing slavery. That apology is bull crap; it is to keep negroes asleep, because for decades we have been speaking about slavery and all the evil the Roman Catholic Church did and is doing. An apology is only an apology if there is justice and restitution. If you steal my house and my land and come and say you are sorry while you are still living in my house on my land, your apology means nothing; if you were really sorry you would give me back my house and my land. A murderer who says he is sorry still has to do his time: justice always has to come forth. We are the only people where somebody can say sorry and nobody thinks about justice. The law is that if you steal from someone you must make restitution, and these popes have the Bible; they are supposed to understand that.

It is much more than the transatlantic slave trade. By the papal bulls of the Doctrine of Discovery the Roman Catholic Church gave the Europeans a permit to take whatever land they found that was not held by Christians, their white Christianity, and to call it nobody’s land. That is how Africa, the New World, the Caribbean and Australia were colonized, the indigenous people reduced to mere occupants, and the land stolen; the same doctrine was used in the United States to displace the North American Indians. The Catholic Church ripped the children of Gad, the North American Indians, from their parents into residential schools, indoctrinated them with Christian lies, abused them and murdered thousands of them, and Gad had no power to take their children out. They still hold all that land. If the Pope were really sorry, he would give back the land. To hell with your apology: our God is going to return and judge, and we will see justice and restitution.

“Because he hath oppressed and hath forsaken the poor”: that is what the white man did; he oppressed the poor. “because he hath violently taken away an house which he builded not”: he violently took away people’s houses that he never built. So the restitution for stealing people’s houses and lands is that he has to give up everything he has, all the wealth he accumulated over these centuries. That is God’s judgment.

“Surely he shall not feel quietness in his belly”: he will not be at peace. “he shall not save of that which he desired”: all those riches, he will not be able to save them for himself. “There shall none of his meat be left; therefore shall no man look for his goods.”

“In the fulness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits: every hand of the wicked shall come upon him.” Every hand of the wicked shall come upon the white man. That is what is going to happen to America: Saudi Arabia, Russia, Persia which is Iran, China.

precepts.why:
The restitution is in Haggai too, at the building of the temple. “I will shake the heavens, and the earth, and the sea, and the dry land; And I will shake all nations”: that is the third woe, when the Lord destroys all nations. “and the desire of all nations shall come”: the desire of all nations is gold, silver, pearls, the riches that they have.

“and I will fill this house with glory”: this house is the third temple. The Lord will fill it with glory, meaning it will be beautiful, because all the gold, the silver and the riches these nations have been stealing and storing are coming back to us. “The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the Lord of hosts”: all the silver on this earth, and all the gold these white people have, God says is his.

“The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former”: the latter house is the third temple that is going to be built, and it will be greater than the temple Solomon built, glorious, because the nations are going to bring their wealth and their gold. So the restitution is everything they have; that is reparation. And everything means gold and silver and precious things, real wealth, not the US dollar, not paper money.

“ye shall eat the riches of the Gentiles”: all their riches are going to belong to us; we are going to eat their food. “and in their glory shall ye boast yourselves”: all the gold they have, we are going to boast ourselves in it. Give me that gold chain; where did you get that gold from? You have been hiding it. Give me that.

Another scripture says the way they will show they are subject to us is by bringing their gold. That is the restitution of Job 20: not an apology, but all their riches brought to Israel.

sense.text:
“All that found them have devoured them: and their adversaries said, We offend not”. That is what the white man did. All the nations that found us devoured us, and then turned around and said, we did not offend, we did nothing wrong. “because they have sinned against the Lord”: because you Israelites, you negroes, keep breaking God’s laws and sinning against God, God made this happen to you, so we did not offend. That is the white man saying he has not offended in colonizing, enslaving and destroying the twelve tribes of Israel. And the hope of our fathers is “the habitation of justice, even the Lord”.

This is how to deal with these damn Edomites who say we have a victim mentality, a victim culture. When we speak about slavery, lynching and the institutions of oppression set up throughout the whole planet, they say: pick yourself up by your bootstraps, it’s been fifty years, you are supposed to be doing better like us white people. But when the Jewish man talks about the Holocaust, do they tell him that is a victim mentality? It is like a woman telling her rapist, you raped me, and the rapist saying, get over it, you got a victim mentality. She was a victim and she wants justice. Here is the oppressor telling the oppressed to stop acting like a victim.

When we came together in Tulsa and built Black Wall Street, they destroyed it. When we try, they destroy it, and then tell us to stop acting like a victim. They set up Jim Crow, hunted us, lynched us, raped our women, and set up institutions to keep us from progressing. We don’t want anything from white people; we don’t want them to help us do anything. But we will let them know all the evil they have done, and that judgment is coming to them from God, the creator of the heavens and the earth, the God of the twelve tribes of Israel. You are the damn oppressor.

precepts.why:
“Feed the flock of the slaughter”: the flock of the slaughter is us, the twelve tribes of Israel. We are being slaughtered; we are being oppressed. “Whose possessors slay them”: our possessors are the nations ruling over us, and they slay us. “and hold themselves not guilty”: they say, forget about it, stop being a victim; yes, we murdered you and brought you over here and lynched you and did all this evil to you, but get over it, it was just fifty years ago. It makes no damn sense.

They say they are not guilty for all that evil, but we charge them in the name of the Lord: you are guilty. Guilty of kidnapping, guilty of murder, guilty of theft, and you will be judged for every last one of the wicked, genocidal things you have done on this earth, and for all the land you stole. The Lord God, the creator of this earth, is going to judge you for that. Thus saith the Lord.

“and they that sell them say, Blessed be the Lord; for I am rich”: that is what the white men say, because they did it in the name of the Lord, in the name of white Jesus. The Roman Catholic Church set up the edicts to enslave and colonize Africa and the New World. “and their own shepherds pity them not”: our own shepherds had no mercy and never helped us.

So concerning that victim mentality: we are victims, we are prisoners, we are being oppressed, and the white man is the oppressor, and when we point it out he tells us to stop being a damn victim. You cannot tell a woman who was raped to get over it. The system was set up to oppress us. They brought drugs into our communities, pushed rap music and sexualized everything; everything you see happening in our community is by design to keep us in the midst of sin. They brought the drugs in and then set up the war on drugs and the prison pipeline, and millions of our brothers ended up in prison and dead. They set up an oppressive system to keep us destroyed, and when we complain they say stop acting like a victim. We are the victims, and our God is going to come and vindicate us.

sense.text:
“And it was given unto him to make war with the saints”. Many think that what the Roman Catholic Church did was just enslave the negroes and bring slaves from Africa. No: it was war, war to destroy the twelve tribes that were living all over Africa and here in the New World. The first slaves came from Spain: they conquered our people who were ruling over there, the Moors; when they finished with us there they went to the New World, and then to Africa. They made war with us in South America, in the New World, in Africa and in Europe. It was war to conquer the lands we were living in and to destroy us as a people: they took our nationality and our identity. So when the white man says he is sorry: give us back our nationality, our identity and our land. Now they call themselves Christians, and they are not the original Christians; they call themselves Jews, and they are not the original Jews.

“and to overcome them”: they overcame us and made us slaves. Slavery was war.

They say black people sold black people into slavery. But the Roman Catholic Church made the edicts and laws legalizing slavery before they ever went to Africa. Slavery was a system set up by Christianity, by white Europeans to conquer Africa, not by tribesmen in Africa, and they had black people fighting among each other, the same way they set us against each other today in South Africa. There was always some form of slavery, like a man who owes money working it off, but not abuse and oppression. Chattel slavery, where your children and great-grandchildren are all slaves after you, is different from any slavery ever set up on this earth, and it was institutionalized by the Pope, by Christianity. If these Christians are sorry, give back all the land you stole.

“and power was given him over all kindreds, and tongues, and nations.”

“And all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him”: everybody started worshipping the white man as Christ and Saviour. “whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world”: because the names of the nations are not written, they will worship the beast; they will worship the white man as Christ and Saviour, and as the Jews.

This is the judgment, the justice, for the verses above. They made war with the saints and overcame us, so: “He that leadeth into captivity shall go into captivity: he that killeth with the sword must be killed with the sword.” He that leads the saints into captivity shall go into captivity; he that kills the saints with the sword will be killed with the sword.

“Here is the patience and the faith of the saints”: this is what the saints are patiently waiting for, and what they believe. If you are a saint, you want vengeance. You want justice for what was done to your forefathers, and that is what you are waiting on.

This opens the teaching of God, purpose and sacrifice. We all must understand who our God is. In understanding who your God is, you will understand your purpose, and in understanding your purpose, you will have to make sacrifices.

“I have nourished and brought up children”: the children God nourished and brought up are the twelve tribes of Israel, you so-called blacks and Hispanics. “and they have rebelled against me”: we rebelled against our God.

“The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master’s crib: but Israel doth not know”. An ox knows his owner, and the ass knows where his master’s crib is, but Israel does not know who his master is. Our master is our God, and we do not know who our God is, and we do not know where our land is. “my people doth not consider”: we do not even consider where our land is.

You cannot separate God and nation; God and nation go hand in hand. If you forget your God, you will forget your nation, and that is what happened to us as a people: we don’t know who our God is, so we don’t know our nation. The Arabs have their god in Islam; the Chinese have Buddha, and they have their land, China; the white man’s god is the white image of Christ, and his land is wherever he wants to take. This verse says we will forget who we are, forget who our God is, and forget where our home is.

precepts.why:
“Hath a nation changed their gods, which are yet no gods?” The nations’ gods are no gods, but nations and their god go hand in hand. Have the Chinese changed their god? Have the Japanese changed their gods? Have the Arabs changed their gods? No. “but my people have changed their glory for that which doth not profit”: we as a people, our nation, have changed our God, our glory, for what does not profit us. Christianity and Islam do not profit us. Christianity is the colonizer religion, built on white supremacy. We are the children of Israel, the original, the people Christ came and died for. Christ was a black man, and reading right through the Bible, the apostles were all black men.

So we must know who our God is and we must know where our land is, because our God and our nation, which is our land, go hand in hand. You cannot say you know God and not know what nation you are from. From the foundation that God always says he is the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the God of Israel; right through the Bible you will never hear him say he is the God of the Chinese. Understand who Israel is and where Israel’s land is, and then you will understand who your God is. Every nation has kept its god, but we changed our glory, and the reason we are in this condition today is that we forgot our God.

sense.text: “For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth”: they that enslaved and destroyed us required us to make mirth, to sing. “saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion.”

“If I forget thee, O Jerusalem”: this is David speaking, and David will come back in the future; that is why he said this. “let my right hand forget her cunning.” What do you do with your right hand? What is the Israelite man’s job on this earth? To serve God and keep his laws. The Lord said the children of Israel are servants unto him; that is our whole duty on this earth, to be servants unto God and not unto anyone else. If you forget Jerusalem, your nation, you will forget what your right hand is supposed to be doing: serving God.

That is what happened to us in slavery. Because we forgot Jerusalem, we forgot our God. We did not know that land is ours, so we did not know we are the children of Israel, and the right hand we used to serve God, keeping the commandments and praising him, has forgotten its cunning. Your God and your nation go hand in hand.

“If I do not remember thee, let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth”: you cannot talk with your tongue cleaving to the roof of your mouth. If you don’t remember that Jerusalem is your land, you will not be able to teach God’s word. The first thing you must learn to understand this book is who you are: you must know that you are an Israelite before you can start teaching this Bible, because God only showed his word unto Israel. You cannot read this Bible thinking you are some other people and understand it; you have to read it with the understanding that it is talking about you, the children of Israel.

“if I prefer not Jerusalem above my chief joy”: Jerusalem is supposed to be your chief joy.

“Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem”: remember white people, Lord. “who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.” David was not there when Edom said that, but David was a prophet, and the Lord showed him in a vision Edom destroying Jerusalem: he saw 70 AD when the Romans came, and saw them helping the Babylonians. That is why David says, Lord, remember what white people did to your people. It also shows who played the role in making us forget Jerusalem as our chief joy.

“O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed”: the same thing ancient Babylon did is the same thing white people did; that is why Edom is called the daughter of Babylon. That is their judgment: the Lord is going to come and destroy white people for what they have done to us.

“And thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee”. Did Jeremiah ever forget who he was, the heritage God gave him? No. Jeremiah stood stiffly for the Lord. He was cast in prison, and when Nebuchadnezzar came and destroyed Jerusalem, Jeremiah was let go free and lived on in the land, teaching the laws to the people left there. So this speaks of Jeremiah when he comes back in the future. The heritage is your God and your land: Jeremiah came on this earth and forgot who his God is and where his land is.

“and I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not”: did Jeremiah serve his enemies in a land he did not know? The Babylonians did not take Jeremiah into Babylon as a slave. Did Jeremiah know anything about the United States of America? This is Jeremiah here in the last days, serving his enemies in the land of his captivity, as we are serving our enemies in America. “for ye have kindled a fire in mine anger, which shall burn for ever.”

But he will remember who he is. The same way, Jeremiah is here and he remembers that he is an Israelite: he remembers his God, his land, his heritage. Your God and your nation go hand in hand: the Bible blesses the Lord God of Israel, and you will never read where God went to Europe and dealt with white people.

precepts.why:
So we as a people would discontinue from our heritage and not know who our God is. “For the children of Israel shall abide many days”: the many days are 350 years. “without a king”: we had no sovereignty; we were colonized and enslaved. “and without a prince, and without a sacrifice”: without a sacrifice is without religious establishments. For 350 years the white man conquered us, colonized Africa and taught us white Jesus, and taught us white Jesus over here as slaves. There was no establishment teaching us true religion, teaching us about our God; in slavery the white man taught us his lies and his God.

“and without an image”: image is nationality. We would not know our nationality, and we would not know what our God looks like, because your God was created in your image. So for many days we would be without a culture: your God, your nation, your heritage, the feast days and holy days, how you worship your God. That is culture and heritage, and for 350 years we were without it.

sense.text:
“Happy art thou, O Israel: who is like unto thee, O people saved by the Lord”: who is going to be happy? Israel. Everybody is not going to be happy. This is salvation, and Israel is the people saved by the Lord. “the shield of thy help, and who is the sword of thy excellency!” That is our shield and our help.

“and thine enemies shall be found liars unto thee”: the prophecy is that our enemies will be found out to have lied to us, and that is today. All of us in this truth have come to understand it: the white man lied to me; he told me Jesus Christ was white; he lied to me. They lied to us about our culture, about our God, about our nationality, and that is what we are finding out today. As this gospel is taught, it is being found out that the white man has been lying to us for centuries. He calls himself a Jew and calls himself a Christian, which he is not. The white man lied to everybody on the earth; the Pope lied to everybody on the earth.

“and thou shalt tread upon their high places”: that is future prophecy. That is the judgment.

“For if he that cometh preacheth another Jesus”: the white man came and taught another Jesus on the earth, a Jesus with green eyes and pale skin. “whom we have not preached”: the apostles never taught that image of Christ.

White people like to say now that Christ was Middle Eastern. What is the land of Israel called? Canaan. And who was in the land of Canaan? Black people, the Hamitic tribes. The Canaanites and the Philistines we fought were all black people. Christ was living in that region, and everybody in that region was black, blacker than black, not some beige, off colour. Don’t let the white man trick you and fool you.

“or if ye receive another spirit, which ye have not received”: the spirit our people follow in Christianity is another spirit. “or another gospel”: the gospel our people follow on the earth today is another gospel. Revelation calls it the mark of the beast, the image of the beast, the false prophet: Christianity, the religion built on white supremacy. With the other Jesus, the white Jesus, comes another gospel, and that other gospel is white supremacy: worship me, worship the white man.

precepts.why:
The disciples asked Christ, “what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world?” What do we have to look for before he comes and before the end of the world takes place? “For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ”: before the end comes and before Christ returns, many must come in his name. The word Christ means anointed. Who came saying they are the anointed ones? White people. It began in the 1400s, during the Renaissance: many shall come in my name, saying that we are Christians. “and shall deceive many”: billions of people on the earth today have been deceived, calling themselves Christians, worshipping a white man as Christ.

So another nation was going to come and teach another Jesus; that is what we had to look for. Understand that your nation and your God go hand in hand. You must have racial identity: you must be able to identify your God and your race together.

sense.text: “If they sin against thee, (for there is no man that sinneth not,) and thou be angry with them”: God was angry with us. “so that they carry them away captives unto the land of the enemy, far or near”: were we carried captive into the land of our enemies? Yes. We Israelites were carried as slaves into the land of our enemies, all the way here to the Americas, because God was angry with us.

“Yet if they shall bethink themselves”: to bethink yourself is to remember who you are, remember your nation, and in remembering your nation you will remember your God, because your nation and your God go hand in hand. For you to bethink yourself means that you forgot: the children of Israel were to be many days without an image and without a sacrifice, and David said, if I forget thee, O Jerusalem. Now we are reading about us coming back, remembering our land and remembering our God, “in the land whither they were carried captives”.

“and repent”: we must change our lives and stop committing sin. That is the key thing we must do as we wake up and learn that we are the children of Israel. We can’t act the way we used to anymore. We have to change, deal right with each other, and get rid of the fornication, the hatred, the jealousy, the bad mind.

“and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness”: we have sinned and done perversely; that is why we are in these lands of our captivity, why we were brought here as slaves, because we sinned against our God.

“And so return unto thee with all their heart, and with all their soul”: what we have to do is return unto God with all our heart and all our soul. This ain’t no half-stepping thing.

“and pray unto thee toward their land”: where is your land? Are you sure it’s not Africa? Don’t be turning toward Africa and praying toward Africa. And it is not Jamaica, not Trinidad, not South Africa or Nigeria or the other lands we were scattered to. To bethink yourself you have to know where your land is: not the land of your captivity, but your nation. Once you know who your God is, you will know where your land is, because your nation and your God go hand in hand.

So the state of mind we all must have is to be nationalists. Don’t let anybody tell you being a nationalist is wrong: you must love your nation, and a nationalist wants a nation, his land. That is what we are, and what we are doing now is starting a revolution to get back our land. We must turn to God and pray toward our land, “which thou gavest unto their fathers, the city which thou hast chosen”: you must know the city God chose, “and the house which I have built for thy name”.

precepts.why:
“Turn ye unto me, saith the Lord of hosts, and I will turn unto you”: God wants us to turn unto him, and when we turn unto God, God will turn unto us.

“Be ye not as your fathers, unto whom the former prophets have cried, saying, Thus saith the Lord of hosts; Turn ye now from your evil ways, and from your evil doings”. The former prophets went to our fathers and said thus saith the Lord, the same way it is being said today: we are telling our people to turn from their evil ways and stop following Christianity. “but they did not hear, nor hearken unto me”: they did not hearken to the prophets back then, and we can’t be like our forefathers who did not listen to the prophets. Brothers hearing these teachings, listen and turn to God with all your heart.

sense.text: “And now, Israel, what doth the Lord thy God require of thee”: what God requires of us as Israel, knowing that we are the children of Israel. “but to fear the Lord thy God, to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve the Lord thy God with all thy heart and with all thy soul”: God wants us to love him and to serve him. How do we love him?

“To keep the commandments of the Lord”: we serve God and show him we love him by keeping the commandments. That is what God wants us to do; that is what he requires of us. So don’t listen to these dumb Christians following white supremacy who say God’s law is done away with, that you don’t have to keep God’s laws, that you can eat pork and shrimp and live however you want to live. “and his statutes, which I command thee this day for thy good”: for our good.

That is the first part of God, purpose and sacrifice: you must know your God as you come into this truth, and then you must find your purpose.

precepts.why:
“Master, which is the great commandment in the law?” “Thou shalt love the Lord thy God”: whose God? Thy God. That is why God and nation go hand in hand: Christ is saying you shall love the Lord your God, “with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment.”

This was not a new commandment. It was said before, but we never kept it, and we have to learn to do it today. So how do you love God with all your heart, soul and mind? Is it a tingly feeling inside, like these Christians, jumping around and shouting? How do you show God you love him?

“If ye love me, keep my commandments.” Everybody on this planet earth, and their mama and their children, say they love God. Christ says, if you love me, keep my commandments. You have to keep God’s commandments; that is how you show God you love him.

“For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments”. If you want to know how you love God with all your heart, soul and mind, this is the love of God: keep his commandments. We have to keep them with all our heart, soul and mind, willingly, loving to do it, training ourselves to hate evil and love good. It is not just a feeling inside; love is an action word: keeping the commandments, following the dietary laws, keeping the feast days, dealing right with your brothers and sisters.

That starts in your house. When the Bible says to love your neighbour as yourself, that starts first and foremost at home. Married couples: if you hate each other, you hate God. Brothers who hate your wife, sisters who hate your husband: you don’t love God. At one time you had goosebumps and sensations and told each other I love you; how did the love turn into hate all of a sudden, with two babies, talking about a divorce and moving on? Your spouse will get on your nerves sometimes, but God wants us to love each other and deal right with each other. That divorce stuff has to stop. Brothers, deal right with your wife: she is the weaker vessel. Don’t be abusive.

“He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him.” If you say you know God and you don’t keep God’s commandments, you are a damn liar. That is for you stupid Christians saying you don’t have to keep God’s laws, that you don’t have to keep the Sabbath day, that the Sabbath changed to Sunday and you can worship God on whatever day you want. No: God says to remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy.

“But whoso keepeth his word, in him verily is the love of God perfected”: the brothers who keep God’s word are the ones who love God, and they are made perfect. “He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked.” Did Christ keep the Sabbath? Did Christ wear fringes? Did Christ keep the Passover? If you say you love the Lord, you are going to do the same things he did when he walked on this earth. Don’t let these Christians and the white man trick you and fool you.

sense.text:
“when all these things are come upon thee, the blessing and the curse”: the blessings came upon us. We went into the land of Israel and prospered; King David set up the kingdom, Solomon ruled, and we had years of peace. Then the curse: we are living in the curses right now. We are in the land of our captivity, oppressed; our resources and our land are being stolen; our oppressors rule over us.

“and thou shalt call them to mind among all the nations, whither the Lord thy God hath driven thee”: everything God mentioned in Deuteronomy 28 came to pass, and one of the curses was that we would go into slavery on cargo slave ships. Our people are all over the world, in China, in India, in Africa, in the Caribbean islands, calling these curses to mind right now.

“And shalt return unto the Lord thy God, and shalt obey his voice”: we must know our God and obey his voice, and his voice is this Bible, what you are hearing right now, “according to all that I command thee this day”.

“thou and thy children, with all thine heart, and with all thy soul”: God did not say you alone repent. He said you and your children have to turn to him. This is nation; this is family. That is why we tell the brothers we want to see your family: it is not just about you, and a nation starts with family.

“That then the Lord thy God will turn thy captivity, and have compassion upon thee”: when we and our children turn to God with all our heart, soul and mind, he will turn our captivity and have compassion on us. “and will return and gather thee from all the nations”: God is going to gather us from all the nations we have been scattered in. You cannot read that as a Christian and understand it; you must read it as an Israelite, understanding that you were scattered throughout the four corners of the earth in slavery, and that God is going to come and gather you if you turn back to him with all your heart, soul and mind.

After you know your God and know what nation you come from, God will give you purpose. After you know the truth that you are an Israelite and you find your God, God is going to give you purpose.

“a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard”: the vineyard is the nation of Israel, and he went out to look for workers. “he sent them into his vineyard”: he sent them into Israel to work.

“and saw others standing idle in the marketplace”: standing idle means people with no purpose. That is us. We were going to the club, partying, caught up in Christianity’s garbage. We were idle, doing nothing; none of us had purpose.

“Go ye also into the vineyard, and whatsoever is right I will give you”: the Lord called us and said, I have a job for you. Every last one of us in here, God called, and he has a job, a purpose, for us. He hired us. We were idle and without purpose, but God called us, woke us up, hired us and gave us a purpose.

precepts.why: “No man can come to me, except the Father which hath sent me draw him”. You can’t come to Christ unless the Father draws you; you can’t come unless God calls you. If you understand these scriptures, whether you are in the doors of any of the IUIC schools or online at home, the only reason you are able to is that the Lord is drawing you to Christ; the Lord called you here. Even if you were skipping through and saw one of our videos, or somebody on your job said something to you, that is the Father lining you up to draw you in.

sense.text:
“For ye see your calling, brethren”: your calling is your purpose, the job you have to do in this truth. Every last one of us has a job, a mission from the Lord. Do you see your calling? Why did God call you? Every one of you must ask yourself this, because after a while every last one of us should see our calling. If you do not, you haven’t fully understood yourself yet.

“how that not many wise men after the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble, are called”: not many, but some. Paul was a wise man, a Pharisee, one of the elite in society. We will have well-educated brothers come among us, and some mighty, and some noble.

“But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise”: the things everybody thinks are foolish, God has chosen, to confound the people who think they are wise and understand what the Bible is talking about. God is going to use us to confound all these Christians. “and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty”: the weak things are us.

“And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen”: the things that are despised are us, the negroes; we are despised and hated. “yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are”: we have no power; we are the weak things of this earth. But God says he will use us to destroy the things that are, to destroy governments and societies on this earth, with our teachings.

“That no flesh should glory in his presence”: God does this so none of us can say, I did this, I am so smart, that is why I understand the Bible. That is what usually runs through the heads of the very educated: I went to college, I went to theology school, that is why I understand. But if you didn’t go to theology school and you are confounding people who did, you understand it is not you; it is the power of God. When the scriptures are opened and taught in this truth, that is the spirit of the Lord working.

People may look at you and say that person is weak, but God uses the weak things so he can show his power, the things people least expect, so that nobody can glory in themselves. The understanding of the scriptures that we have is the power and the spirit of God.

“But unto every one of us is given grace”: grace means mercy. “according to the measure of the gift of Christ”: Christ gave every last one of us gifts, and your gift goes hand in hand with your calling, your purpose. The gifts God gave you are according to what he wants you to do on this earth.

Every last one of us has gifts, some more than others, but it is for you to see them, and it is the leader’s job to help you cultivate the gift God gave you and stir it up. After you know your God you must find your purpose in this truth, see your calling, and be able to say: this is why God called me. It can take years, but as the gifts develop you understand what the Lord wants you to do.

“When he ascended up on high, he led captivity captive, and gave gifts unto men”: God gave gifts to every last one of us, and your calling goes with your gifts. A wife who never learned to sew began making garments, self-taught, when her husband came into the truth and asked her for one; that was a gift from God. Captain Zev never learned IT, and he started dealing with all the IT work. Those gifts are to build God’s nation. If the Lord made it so you went to school to be a doctor, that was not for you to get rich in this world; it is for you to help your people. Sisters cooking and serving the brothers, being hospitable, and those who help financially: those are gifts too.

“And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers”: some of us Christ made apostles, and some prophets; some of the brothers in IUIC are prophets. Some are evangelists, and there are different forms of evangelism: travelling to different states, different countries, different boroughs, going forth and teaching the word. Some the Lord made pastors, and some teachers.

“For the perfecting of the saints”: why did God give everybody these gifts? Not for us to glorify ourselves. The gifts of a teacher, a prophet, an evangelist are to help the brothers become perfect through the scriptures. A class like this one, on God, purpose and sacrifice, is not taught for no reason: it is to build the brothers up, help them find their purpose and see their calling, and know they are not here for no reason. That is the leader’s job, and as you grow in the spirit it becomes your job too, to build up the men who come after you and help them become perfect.

“for the work of the ministry”: the Lord hired men who were idle, brought them in and gave us a job. That is why God gave us gifts, and eventually every last one of us has to see our calling. “for the edifying of the body of Christ”: to give the body understanding, to edify and exalt it.

precepts.why:
“not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think”: as you grow in this truth and God gives you gifts, don’t think of yourself more highly than you ought to. That is why the Lord usually deals with the base, so no man can glory in his presence: gifts can puff you up. Stay humble, because the reason God gave you those gifts was to build his nation and benefit his people. “but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith”: God gave each of us a different measure of faith, a different amount of gifts, so we are not to envy or be jealous of each other.

“For as we have many members in one body, and all members have not the same office”: we don’t all have the same office; one brother can do what another cannot. God gave us different gifts, and we have to learn to work together and see the best in each other. We are building a nation, setting up a government: in that nation there is an army, but there are a lot of other things that need to be set up besides the army. “So we, being many, are one body in Christ”.

“Having then gifts differing according to the grace that is given to us”: everybody does not have the same purpose, and each one must see his gifts and his calling. “whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith”: prophesy according to the measure God gave you. You may see the Bishop or the Deacons go into some things and think you can go there too; if you are not there yet, don’t try to go there. Take your time with it.

“Or ministry, let us wait on our ministering”: that is the key. Your calling does not come as you come into the truth. It comes after you overcome your regular sins and God gives you gifts; when you get that increase, then you understand your ministry. Every one of you has a ministry in this truth. It may take time, and the leaders’ job is to help cultivate you and help you find your ministry, your purpose. After you find your God, your God will give you gifts and a purpose. “or he that teacheth, on teaching”: some of your purpose might be to teach, some to prophesy, and God may give some of us more than one of these gifts.

“he that giveth, let him do it with simplicity”: giving and helping is a gift. “he that ruleth, with diligence”: some of you may be leaders; do it diligently. “he that sheweth mercy, with cheerfulness”: be cheerful in showing mercy, not grudging about having to forgive a brother.

“Let love be without dissimulation”: we should not be trying to break each other down, especially when you see a brother has a gift you don’t have. “Abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good. Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love”: we must have brotherly love toward each other.

sense.text:
“And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose”: we are called according to God’s purpose, and God has a purpose for every last one of us: the brothers on IT, on the audio, editing the videos, making the thumbnails, the brothers and sisters on security. You don’t have to have rank to have a purpose. You don’t have to be a soldier, or in the army, to do the work of God. We have programs set up: we need some of you on the medical team, some in the stewardship program. It is a nation we are building.

Rank is for order. Rank is important; it is for structure and order. But some let it get to their heads: rank is not for you to be lord over anybody. You still have to do the work, and there are other things in the nation that we need to work together to get done.

precepts.why: “For many are called, but few are chosen.” What will tell whether you are chosen or not is your actions. If you stay in the midst of adultery and keep doing all types of wickedness, carrying grudges and hatred toward your brothers and sisters, being deceitful, still dealing with hoes, buying prostitutes, God is not going to choose you. He called you, but you are not going to be chosen.

sense.text: “For there must be also heresies among you, that they which are approved may be made manifest among you”: there must be heresies among us. How do you tell who is approved by God? Heresies have to take place.

“Take heed to the ministry which thou hast received in the Lord”: take heed to your ministry. Your ministry is your calling, your purpose, and we all have one. “that thou fulfil it”: we all have to make sure we fulfil our calling, our ministry. Eventually every last one of us will figure it out and see why God called us.

“give diligence to make your calling and election sure”: the purpose God called you for, you have to make sure, and only you can make your calling and election sure. How? By keeping the commandments, dealing right with each other, and understanding your purpose. Sit down and ask yourself: why did God call me into this truth? What can I do to help build this nation? What gifts do I have?

There are a lot of things that have to be done, and we have to take it to another level and separate ourselves from this system. Why are we buying chickens from the store? Why, every Passover, are we buying lambs from these farmers? Why don’t we have our own land, talking about being a nation within a nation? Are we really a nation if we have to depend on everybody for everything? God is going to give some of you the gifts to go into farming. Everybody has a purpose in this truth, but it is up to you to see your calling and your purpose and figure it out.

As you find your purpose in this truth, Satan is going to come after you, and a lot of us will have to make sacrifices. You are not going to serve God without having to make sacrifices.

“Behold, we have forsaken all, and followed thee; what shall we have therefore?” Peter forsook everything to follow after Christ. Do you have that state of mind, willing to make that sacrifice and forsake everything to follow after Christ? Kanye wasn’t willing to do that. Nick Cannon wasn’t willing to do that; they would lose billions of dollars. Are you willing to lose everything to follow after Christ? That is what this truth is about.

“If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple.” You cannot be Christ’s disciple if you are not willing to sacrifice your family, and even your own life.
“And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple”: Christ says you can’t be his disciple if you aren’t willing to carry your cross, your burdens, and follow after him.

“which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost”: you had better sit down and count the cost. “all that behold it begin to mock him, Saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish.” People will mock you if you start in this truth and give up. Brothers and sisters, you talk all that good talk to your family, telling them they are wicked, and then you go back: they are going to laugh at you.

“So likewise, whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple”: this is the point of hating father, mother and children. If you are not willing to forsake all you have and make sacrifices, you cannot be Christ’s disciple, and that includes your own life. You have to be willing to die for what you believe in.
